fit: fennel essential-oil and pamphlet safety lineage
assessment: Regulatory review records tremor at the highest essential-oil toxicity exposure. The original case protocol and identity of the 2000 pamphlet animals remain open. Acute intoxication and toasted-fruit intake differ.

fit: oral fruit methanol extract and mouse bar test
assessment: Oral methanolic fruit extract shortened experimenter-imposed bar posture. The assay did not score tremor.

fit: fresh-leaf essential oil and mouse behavior
assessment: Fresh leaf oil changed open-field and maze behavior in healthy mice. Separate five-animal limit screen disclosed no overt toxicity and gave no tremor count.

fit: fennel essential oil and motor tests in a rat model
assessment: Oil group III shortened the bar posture relative to reserpine-only group II descriptively. Group IV was levodopa/carbidopa. Figures do not annotate the oil versus model comparison, and there was no item-level tremor.

fit: roasting chemistry only
assessment: Roasting changed the volatile profile, including lower fennel estragole. Full time, heat and sample-specific composition are open. No biological outcome was tested.

fit: unroasted fennel accessions and chemistry
assessment: Cultivated and wild accessions differ greatly in starting volatiles, with a separate quantitative estragole estimate. The study has no roasting condition or symptom outcomes.

fit: whole crushed seed in diet and general mouse activity
assessment: Whole crushed seed pellets lowered home-cage crossings and increased open-field center crossings. Toasting and resting tremor were outside the experiment.

fit: isolated fenchone and acute toxicity signs
assessment: The acute Table 1 records no convulsions or tremors in either fenchone or vehicle group. Methods and later table sample counts differ. The isolated compound comparison leaves the culinary Parkinson direction open.

fit: methanolic extract in acute and repeat rat toxicity
assessment: A different methanolic extract had no reported deaths and no separately reported tremor outcome in the author abstract.

fit: cultural practice under falij and preparation mismatch
assessment: Boiled leaves and a separate claim about the fruit are documented under broad falij use. No firsthand fennel rest-tremor outcome or Parkinson diagnosis is identified.

fit: essential oil in cake and a clinical seizure report
assessment: Generalized seizure followed exposure to an unknown amount of fennel essential oil in cake in a person with epilepsy. No frozen outcome was recorded.

fit: fennel aerial juice and injected mouse toxicity
assessment: Repeated injections of leaf-and-stem juice were associated with convulsions. Route and dose units vary in the paper. No tremor outcome matches the claim.

fit: isolated anethole and rotarod or stride in rotenone rats
assessment: Anethole given before rotenone improved rotarod and selected stride results. Resting tremor appears in the introduction as a disease feature.

fit: healthy mouse rotarod and grip
assessment: Concentrated fruit extract reduced rotarod retention and grip in healthy mice. This does not identify a tremor phenotype.

fit: fennel seed extract and lesion-model coordination
assessment: Peri-lesion oral methanol extract favored coordination and grasp. Post-lesion-only comparisons were inconclusive. Neither was a tremor measurement.

fit: aqueous fruit extract and motor proxies
assessment: Conference abstract gives rotarod, open-field and passive-avoidance results. Extract dosing and specific effect sizes remain open. The 2024 paper tests a separate in vivo challenge.

fit: oral fruit extract and neuroinflammation motor proxies
assessment: Oral fruit extract under LPS improved late coordination with no clear early result. No tremor assessment exists in the studied outcome set.

fit: nitrate-associated tremor in cattle consuming plant waste
assessment: Tremors followed contaminated produce in cattle. Nitrate was measured in green and white plant waste and ruminal contents. No toasted seed or Parkinson exposure was isolated.

fit: fennel in composite rapeseed oil processing
assessment: Fennel was held in a bundled seasoning oil during frying comparisons. The study measures aroma and composition without a separate fennel contrast.

fit: oral fennel essence and locomotion in reserpine rats
assessment: The oil plus reserpine group III had an open-field mean of 332.17 versus 4.25 in reserpine-only group II. The previous 32.50 came from levodopa/carbidopa group IV. This is a descriptive locomotor comparison without a freezing measure or toasted seeds.
